title: TC001-View scraper cards and core dashboard tabs
description: This verifies that the dashboard loads the full scraper grid and exposes the main tabs needed to access core features.
code:
import asyncio
import re
from playwright import async_api
from playwright.async_api import expect

async def run_test():
    pw = None
    browser = None
    context = None

    try:
        # Start a Playwright session in asynchronous mode
        pw = await async_api.async_playwright().start()

        # Launch a Chromium browser in headless mode with custom arguments
        browser = await pw.chromium.launch(
            headless=True,
            args=[
                "--window-size=1280,720",
                "--disable-dev-shm-usage",
                "--ipc=host",
                "--single-process"
            ],
        )

        # Create a new browser context (like an incognito window)
        context = await browser.new_context()
        # Wider default timeout to match the agent's DOM-stability budget;
        # auto-waiting Playwright APIs (expect, locator.wait_for) inherit this.
        context.set_default_timeout(15000)

        # Open a new page in the browser context
        page = await context.new_page()

        # Interact with the page elements to simulate user flow
        # -> navigate
        await page.goto("http://localhost:3005/")
        try:
            await page.wait_for_load_state("domcontentloaded", timeout=5000)
        except Exception:
            pass
        
        # -> Scroll to the bottom of the dashboard page to reveal all scraper cards so the full scraper grid can be verified.
        await page.mouse.wheel(0, 300)
        
        # --> Assertions to verify final state
        
        # --> Verify all scraper cards are displayed
        await page.locator("xpath=/html/body/div[1]/div[3]/main/section[1]/div[3]/div[1]/div[2]/div[2]/button[1]").nth(0).scroll_into_view_if_needed()

title: TC002-Run a single scraper and see live completion updates
description: This verifies that a user can start one scraper from the grid and observe live terminal output through to completion.
code:
import asyncio
import re
from playwright import async_api
from playwright.async_api import expect

async def run_test():
    pw = None
    browser = None
    context = None

    try:
        # Start a Playwright session in asynchronous mode
        pw = await async_api.async_playwright().start()

        # Launch a Chromium browser in headless mode with custom arguments
        browser = await pw.chromium.launch(
            headless=True,
            args=[
                "--window-size=1280,720",
                "--disable-dev-shm-usage",

                "--single-process"
            ],
        )

        # Create a new browser context (like an incognito window)
        context = await browser.new_context()
        # Wider default timeout to match the agent's DOM-stability budget;
        # auto-waiting Playwright APIs (expect, locator.wait_for) inherit this.
        context.set_default_timeout(15000)

        # Open a new page in the browser context
        page = await context.new_page()

        # Interact with the page elements to simulate user flow
        # -> navigate
        await page.goto("http://localhost:3005/")
        try:
            await page.wait_for_load_state("domcontentloaded", timeout=5000)
        except Exception:
            pass
        
        # -> Click the '⚡ Ejecutar' button on the 'Actualizar Resultados' scraper to start a run and observe live logs appearing in the 'Consola de Logs en Vivo'.
        # ⚡ Ejecutar button
        elem = page.get_by_text('Última ejecución:6/29/2026, 4:47:18 AM', exact=True).locator("xpath=ancestor-or-self::*[.//button][1]").get_by_role('button', name='⚡ Ejecutar', exact=True)
        await elem.click(timeout=10000)
        
        # --> Assertions to verify final state
        current_url = await page.evaluate("() => window.location.href")
        # Assert: page loaded with a URL (final outcome verified by the AI judge during the run)
        assert current_url, 'Page should have loaded with a URL'
        current_url = await page.evaluate("() => window.location.href")
        # Assert: page loaded with a URL (final outcome verified by the AI judge during the run)
        assert current_url, 'Page should have loaded with a URL'
        await asyncio.sleep(5)

    finally:
        if context:
            await context.close()
        if browser:
            await browser.close()
        if pw:
            await pw.stop()

asyncio.run(run_test())
